input.quote: 3.4 HDI's General Manager (as hereinafter defined), may upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect the records of the Company's General Manager reasonably related to the calculation of such payments during the Company's normal business hours. The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI.
input.rationale: Section 3.4 is the only provision binding the Company to an audit/inspection right (no other audit, records or verification clause exists in the Agreement). It already meets two fallback elements on their material terms: inspections require no less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice (exceeding the 15-day floor) and HDI bears the inspection cost unconditionally (better than "unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent"); it is also limited to payment-calculation records during normal business hours. But it imposes no frequency limit, so HDI could inspect repeatedly, failing the fallback once-per-year element and edging toward walk-away territory. We propose the single minimal edit adding a once-per-year cap. We have not pursued the preferred independent-auditor, confidentiality, off-site or no-systems-access elements, as fallback is the selected target and the notice and cost terms already sit at or above it.

proposal.summary: Cap HDI's records inspection right at once per year in §3.4.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 3.4 gives HDI an unlimited number of inspections of our records; our playbook fallback requires audits to be limited to once per year. We have added that frequency cap and left the existing 30 days' notice, business-hours and HDI-borne cost terms untouched.
